newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council calls for halt to Jerusalem violence.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council calls for halt to Jerusalem violence.

text.p: Security Council members expressed concern on Wednesday at the situation in Jerusalem and Ramallah, where Palestinians were killed and wounded in clashes with Israeli troops, and called on all sides to exercise restraint and avoid further violence.
The appeal was made in a statement read to reporters by council President Alfredo Lopes Cabral of Guinea-Bissau after closed-door council consultations.

He had earlier conferred with the Palestine Liberation Organisation's U.N. observer, Nasser al-Kidwa, who urged action to get Israel to rescind the opening of a new entrance to a pedestrian tunnel in Jerusalem's Old City near Moslem and Jewish holy places.
Palestinian demonstrators clashed with Israeli troops and police in Jerusalem and the nearby West Bank town of Ramallah, resulting in some of the bloodiest clashes since PLO rule began two years ago.
Cabral said council members, after comments by Egypt's ambassador Nabil Elaraby, himself a member of the 15-nation council, "expresed their concern about the situation in Jerusalem and Ramallah."
"The members of the council urge all sides to move quickly to restore calm and to exercise restraint and avoid further violence," Cabral added.
Al-Kidwa had earlier sent letters to Cabral and to Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali saying he hoped the council would "take the necessary steps" to get Israel to rescind its action.

The violence was sparked by the opening of an entrance to a tunnel designed to display excavated parts of the Western Wall, or Wailing Wall, Judaism's holiest shrine, which is also a retaining wall for a mosque compound known as Haram al-Sharif on which stands al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest shrine.
